chapter: Cab Calloway's band: road, arrangers and shows
title: Arrangers for Cab: Andy Gibson and Chappy Willet
summary: Andy Gibson wrote every part without a score, and Chappy Willet was the show arranger of Holiday for Strings.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well tell me about some of those guys. Who was Andy Gibson?

Andy Gibson was a great arranger. I think he‟s from Cleveland, Ohio. I don‟t know what he played except it was trumpet. But he was the kind of arranger of the old school. He wrote every part. He didn‟t write a score. He sat down and [unintelligible] write a second or third alto and [unintelligible] it would be right.
That‟s some kind of mind, man [laugh].

That‟s right, he had that kind of mind. He was beautiful, very quiet little guy and Charlie Bonnet and everybody used him because he was a magnificent arranger. In fact he did [unintelligible] for me.

Chappy Willard was our show business arranger. His music was flair. He had big introductions and some semi-classical thing like Holiday For Strings was a big deal. He wrote us an arrangement of Holiday For Strings that just tore the house down.
